newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine March inflation rise led by food.
newsitem.headline: Philippine March inflation rise led by food.

text.p: A year-on-year 4.8 percent gain in the Philippines' March inflation rate from 4.4 percent in February was led by an increase in food prices, a report from the National Statistics Office (NSO) said on Friday.

Food, beverages and tobacco make up the biggest portion of the index, at 58.47 percent. Within that sector, the year-on-year inflation for food alone rose to 1.7 percent in March from 0.6 percent in February, the NSO said.
On a month-on-month basis, the overall inflation rate rose 0.8 percent in March, following a 0.4 percent gain in February.
From February to March, food, beverages and tobacco gained 0.9 percent compared with zero growth in February from January.
On a month-on-month basis, the price of rice, a major food component, rose by 1.6 percent in March from 0.3 percent in February.
The overall year-on-year March inflation rate of 4.8 percent was slightly above a Reuters poll done earlier this week that produced a consensus of 4.62 percent.
Economists had expected little price pressure from commodities or energy.
The latest figure was still far below the year-on-year 11.8 percent inflation surge reported in March 1996, when a severe rice shortage pushed up prices.
